title: Orbit cadence: weekly build windows, RC fencing, and release automation playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and automate a repeatable weekly release orbit for Redwood runtime and platform components that combines a constrained build window, deterministic RC fencing rules, automated release-note composition, and an upgrade-safe rollout path for LTS and non-LTS channels.

Why: Current weekly cuts vary by team and rely on ad-hoc notes and manual gating. This creates churn during rollouts, inconsistent RC tagging, and makes regressions harder to trace across channels. A consistent orbit reduces toil, makes rollbacks deterministic, and enables programmatic release-note and changelog generation tied to test gates.

Scope: runtime binaries, serving runtime kernels, console minor releases, and infra orchestration agents. Not in this ticket: major-version policy changes and package manager plumbing (handled in ENG-11800).

Success criteria (acceptance):
- A documented weekly build window and RC fencing policy exists in Confluence and is approved by Eng Leads and Product.
- CI pipeline (ci/release/orbit-cut) produces a candidate RC tag and JSON metadata artifact (rc_metadata.json) that includes committish, artifact checksums, failing-test summary, and canary cohort config.
- Automated release-notes composer (job release/notes/compose) aggregates PR summaries, linked issues, and curated highlight bullets; output attaches to the RC tag and Slack #release-notes.
- Two-stage rollout gate enforced: integration gating (automated test pass thresholds) and staged canary rollout controlled by Redfall (internal rollout service).
- Upgrade tooling validates in-place KV-cache migrations and reports incompatibilities before promoting RC to LTS channel.

Deliverables:
1) Playbook: "Orbit cadence and RC fencing" with build window, cut checklist, escalation contacts.
2) CI changes: new jobs for rc-metadata generation, changelog composer, and rc-fencing-enforcer.
3) Rollout config: default canary cohorts and rollback criteria.
4) Release notes automation: mapping of PR labels to release sections (Fixes, Improvements, Breaking Changes) and enrichers for perf numbers.

Out of scope: permanent changes to customer-facing version schema, shipping schedule negotiation with sales (handled by PM team).
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Patel: Kickoff meeting held with Runtime, Infra, and DX. Agreed on a 3-hour weekly build window (Tuesday 02:00-05:00 UTC). Action: engineering to draft fencing rules by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-11 Liam Chen: Drafted initial RC fencing rules. Key point: any PR that introduces non-backwards-compatible kernel changes must be merged into a feature branch and excluded from the weekly RC unless explicitly approved. See draft doc: /confluence/release-orbit/drafts.
2026-03-12 Runtime Lead (Marcos Alvarez): Recommended adding a pre-cut KV-cache migration smoke test to CI. Estimation: +6m average per RC for the smoke suite. Approved to include as gating metric.

2026-03-13 EngOps (Priya Kapoor): Prototype ci/release/orbit-cut job wired to tag: refs/tags/orbit-rc-YYYYMMDD-<n>. Generated rc_metadata.json example stored in s3://redwood-release-meta/orbit/11427/.

2026-03-14 Liam Chen: POC for release-notes composer submitted (PR gh/rw/release-notes-composer#224). Composer maps labels (release-note/major, release-note/skip, release-note/experimental) to sections and includes linked Linear issues. Needs QA for long PR titles truncation logic.

2026-03-14 Aisha Patel: Decision log: Use two-week LTS promotion delay by default after RC stabilizes; promotion requires at least 48 hours of production canary traffic with no SLO regressions greater than 0.5%.
2026-03-14 Eng Lead Review (Sofia Nguyen): Requested explicit rollback playbook and runbook steps for kernel hotfixes and a checklist for datastore schema compatibility checks.
